title: MSP-MVS Multi-granularity Segmentation Prior Guided Multi-View Stereo

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction paragraphs beginning “Therefore, we propose TSAR-MVS” through the subsequent TSAR-MVS contribution list
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper is titled and abstracted as “MSP-MVS,” whose stated mechanism is multi-granularity segmentation-prior-guided patch deformation, anchor equidistribution, and iterative local search. However, the introduction abruptly states “we propose TSAR-MVS” and describes a fundamentally different post-processing pipeline: confidence/disparity outlier filtering, superpixel RANSAC planarization, weighted-median filtering, and Roberts/Hough textureless-aware segmentation. It then gives contributions for that TSAR-MVS pipeline. These cannot both be the proposed method of the same paper, and the document does not explain any relationship or composition between them.

predicted_errors.error_location: MSP-MVS method motivation paragraphs stating “Semantic-SAM can achieve panoramic segmentation at any granularity,” cited as “Semantic-SAM (Kirillov et al. 2023)”
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Kirillov et al. (2023) is the Segment Anything (SAM) paper, not Semantic-SAM. Semantic-SAM is a separate work and is absent from the bibliography. Moreover, the claimed semantic-awareness and arbitrary-granularity semantic segmentation capability is not properly attributable to the cited SAM reference. The method’s key source model is therefore misidentified and uncited.

predicted_errors.error_location: Experiment description: paragraph beginning “Experiments on extensive datasets...” versus later evaluation paragraph
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper claims that experiments on “the ETH3D high-resolution dataset, Tanks & Temples dataset and Strecha dataset” demonstrate the method. Later it says “We evaluate our work on ETH3D benchmark ... and Tanks & Temples benchmark,” and all subsequent qualitative and quantitative-result discussion concerns only ETH3D and Tanks & Temples. No Strecha protocol, results, comparison, or analysis is provided in the supplied full text. Thus the stated experimental coverage is inconsistent with the described and reported evaluation.

The ablation claims to remove “aggregation (w/o. Agr.)” and “edge correction (w/o. CRF.).” Yet the MSP-MVS method description never defines a CRF, specifies a CRF-based edge-correction step, gives its inputs/outputs, or explains the aggregation operation sufficiently to identify the ablated component. The only MSP description says that edges are “integrat[ed]” and later “aggregate[d] and correct[ed],” without defining a CRF. Consequently, the reported model and its ablations do not correspond to a reproducibly specified method.

predicted_errors.error_location: MSP-MVS ablation discussion, sentence beginning “Both w/o. Her. and w/o. Agr. produce similar better results than w/o. CRF.”
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The stated comparison says that removing hierarchy or aggregation (“w/o. Her.” and “w/o. Agr.”) gives better results than removing CRF edge correction (“w/o. CRF.”). If so, removing CRF is more damaging, which supports edge correction being more important than either hierarchy or aggregation. The paper instead concludes that multi-granularity prior and aggregation are “equally crucial than edge correction,” which does not follow from, and is directionally contrary to, its own stated ablation ordering.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results and ablation claims throughout the experimental portion
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text repeatedly claims state-of-the-art scores, highest F1/completeness, a less-than-0.3% gap on Tanks & Temples Advanced, competitive runtime, and specific ablation rankings. However, the supplied full paper contains no quantitative-result tables, no numerical benchmark values, no runtime/memory values, no figures, and no ablation table from which these assertions can be verified. Statements such as “Quantitative results ... are respectively presented” refer to absent material. The performance and conclusion claims therefore lack the reported evidence required to support them.
